invariants.statement: Equivalent lower-secondary class labels resolve to the unique real Registro ClassData.id, while duplicate semantic identities fail closed.
A local UDA bound to one real class by an exact stored class name remains selectable even when that display name has no semantic class key; semantic collisions still fail closed.
The teacher uses one coordinated Copilot surface and teacher-first preparation preserves explicit class and UDA authority without inventing targets.
Contextual didactic REVIEW remains local and read-only, requires real evidence, and never fabricates curriculum alignment or a target.
Professional mutations are serialized, persisted before publication, and rejected writes cannot publish success or overwrite later intent.
Every guarded change is mapped to stable invariants and executable evidence; qualification is exact-SHA and the fast compatibility smoke precedes expensive browser regression.

Docente OS teaching projection input is accepted only through the versioned V1 allowlisted contract with valid fingerprint, provenance and professional non-personal content; parsing alone grants no persistence authority.

Accepted Docente OS projections remain inside Planning V2 in the existing encrypted planning record, normalize safely from historical planning state, round-trip through supported backups, and never become canonical Registro UDA records.

Projection acceptance reconciles classes through canonical Registro identity inside the commit-first planning mutation boundary; ambiguity and unresolved identity fail closed, resolved bindings cannot silently retarget, and explicit replacement remains slot-scoped.

Projected Docente OS UDA remain derived read-only professional context under canonical Registro class identity; local UDA retain write authority, projected targets cannot receive Registro professional writes, and collisions or stale bindings fail closed.
Projected UDA may participate as read-only professional context across Copilot, Biblioteca, relevance and REVIEW without gaining local mutation, mission-completion or adoption authority.

Registro consumes the exact qualified shared semantic-memory contract as a vendored local package; the package remains derived/provider-neutral and adds no build-time network or external-registry dependency.

Registro reaches semantic memory only through an explicit session-scoped HTTP loopback boundary: construction and rendering perform no network request, non-loopback endpoints fail before fetch, POST operations require bearer authentication, redirects/caching/credentials are disabled, shared envelopes are validated, connection and synchronization require explicit teacher actions, and the existing local Library fallback remains available when no usable LSM session exists.

Library reuse remains explicitly teacher-triggered through one unified teaching-target selector and explicit PREPARE, REVIEW, or LINK actions; direct actions preserve the selected target and selection alone never opens the reuse surface.

On mobile, the Library Copilot keeps exactly the current PREPARE primary action reachable above the safe area while preserving a single scroll body, desktop layout, explicit consent, authorization and persistence governance.

Local semantic memory activation is explicitly teacher-triggered and zero-token: the browser bootstraps only against HTTP loopback, receives only an ephemeral session capability, persists no LSM secret, performs no automatic synchronization, and keeps semantic memory unavailable until the local session is explicitly activated.
Registro server bind is controlled only by server-side TRAMA_BIND_HOST; hosted default remains 0.0.0.0 and local Android supervision may bind loopback 127.0.0.1 without browser authority.
Professional context is session-only, deterministic and minimised; contradictions fail closed; existing neutral-entry and student-data privacy invariants remain authoritative.

Home/Oggi is a session-only task router: it never infers class context, never persists task intent, preserves expert Home views, and routes only to existing authoritative specialist surfaces after explicit teacher choices.

Prepara is a session-only professional-intent router: it preserves the explicitly selected class, delegates to existing authoritative preparation surfaces, opens Copilota with class-only prepare intent, and never persists or invents preparation targets.

Conduci is a mobile-first session orchestrator: it preserves the explicitly selected class, resolves lesson context deterministically, keeps rapid observations transient, exposes existing Privacy Shield and specialist tools, hands off explicitly to Registra, and performs no durable professional write.

Registra is a session-only recording orchestrator: it preserves explicit professional context, carries staged lesson evidence without auto-writing it, delegates all durable writes to authoritative specialist surfaces, preserves drafts on failure, and offers Rivedi only after a matching successful durable mutation.

Rivedi is a session-only professional review orchestrator that preserves explicit class and review mission across existing authoritative surfaces, remains non-persistent and descriptive, never decides or auto-writes professional outcomes, and fails closed across class or review-boundary changes.

On mobile an adaptive, compact, accessible Copilota entry occupies the left side above the existing bottom navigation, yields to downward scroll and focused input, returns on upward scroll, and does not interfere with direct Vault lock or professional writes. Desktop entry remains unchanged. In professional editing screens every Save/Update/Cancel action must remain unobstructed, and Vault lock controls must occupy a directly accessible header slot instead of a floating content overlay.

Automatic Git-triggered Vercel deployments must remain disabled for the Registro Docente repository until an explicitly approved deployment policy replaces this guard; no main or preview push may implicitly publish school workflows.

The contextual header projection is a pure view-only function: it uses only an explicit authorized route, the provided current class, and verified editing state; it never invents a class, infers an edit from a route, reads storage, mutates professional data or changes navigation authority.

The contextual header save status is a pure view-only projection of verified persistence evidence: a saved state requires a confirmed durable local write and a nonblank operation ID; unresolved failures, even with a missing operation ID, always take precedence over in-flight writes and unrelated successes; transient notifications, route changes, or unverified edits never imply a saved or synchronized state.

The contextual top bar's single brand control opens navigation, never implicitly resets the work session; Oggi is an explicit guarded destination. Privacy and one-tap locking remain separate 48px controls delegated to existing authority, automatic locking stays a controlled secondary drawer setting, and save status is shown only from verified durable-operation evidence. No cloud sync, student data access, new vault authority or automatic destructive professional navigation is introduced.

Real mobile-header wiring delegates lock and auto-lock changes directly to SecureRegistroRoot, does not create duplicate mobile Vault controls or false save confirmations, uses the brand exclusively to open navigation, requires explicit confirmation before the Oggi route resets professional context, and preserves desktop specialist navigation. No actual records are mutated in qualification.

The mobile Tabellone displays one compact accessible row per student and only one expanded detail at a time, with the student report action separate. It preserves per-period and per-type grade calculations, proposed-indicator settings, privacy masking and accessible labels, while the desktop table and all professional persistence remain unchanged. Expansion state is scoped to the current class and no real student data is used in qualification.

Browser/Android Back from a student report must restore the actual previous professional view and class (Tabellone or Analisi) rather than default to the class dashboard. Report entry is recorded in browser history, Forward restores only a student still belonging to the same available class, and student identifiers remain in history.state, never the URL. Cross-class or stale report states fail closed. No teacher record, Vault, lesson, evaluation or analytics calculation is changed.

After browser/Android Back from a student report to its actual origin, only a temporary class-scoped mobile consultative snapshot may restore the previously expanded Tabellone row or Analisi student detail, local filters and approximate scroll. The snapshot is never written to URL, history.state, Secure Local Vault, or persisted professional records. An unrelated route, missing student, class change or protected-name search must not resurrect stale data or expose student names. Report navigation, per-student calculations and desktop grids remain authoritative and unchanged.

On Android/mobile, opening a compact Tabellone student row creates one non-identifying browser-history detail step: first Back collapses the row without leaving the class, second Back returns to the preceding section; Forward and manual collapse preserve coherent steps for the still-current class. Row identities, student names, grades and temporary report-return context never enter the inline history state or the URL. At most one row is expanded, stale or cross-class information cannot revive, report-origin Back remains authoritative, and desktop tables and professional persistence do not change. Explicit navigation to another section, class or Home consumes the transient disclosure step first so Back does not visit duplicate Tabellone entries, while an inline Back/Forward within the same class and surface must preserve the active Rivedi professional session. Concurrent rapid explicit navigation requests must reuse the one pending Back traversal (latest destination wins), never traversing twice. Manual collapse is also delegated to the App-owned serialized queue, so repeated close taps or close followed by explicit navigation never cause multiple Back traversals. A student report requested while an inline Back is pending supersedes earlier navigation or manual-collapse requests; an ordinary report with no pending Back preserves the existing report-return behavior. If opening the student report supersedes an already-pending inline Back, its ephemeral return context must NOT reopen a row after that history step has been consumed; subsequent Back returns to the true prior section.

Specialist evaluation editing in the current class creates a browser-history entry with a session-only opaque evaluation token, while keeping the latest student-report and mobile Tabellone navigation contracts unchanged. Cancel editing discards only volatile changes, returns to Storico and invalidates the canceled editor route. Back/Forward never restores a deleted or cross-class evaluation. Saving changes the browser route only after a confirmed durable commit; no grade, batch or student identity is added to the evaluation URL or history.state.

Programmazione is resolved class-first with fail-closed identity and authority checks; one validated session-only teaching focus carries explicit UDA/lesson context between authoritative specialist surfaces without auto-selection, autosave or schema migration; Docente OS projections remain read-only.

The teacher may explicitly navigate from a ready teacher-professional Library source to the existing Verifiche workspace using only session-local source and active-class references. A pure resolver revalidates classification and active class at departure and arrival; source deletion, revocation and class change fail closed. The destination presents context and requires a second explicit action to open a new unsaved editor; no UDA is chosen by array position and the handoff alone never creates a test, writes a student record, grants Copilot authority, persists a source payload or adds source data to browser history/URL. All existing professional save coordinators and protected mobile routes remain authoritative. The assessment editor now guards modified unsaved drafts across Android Back and explicit navigation, preserves the option to remain or discard, restricts UDA choices and save-time UDA authority to the active class (including short/full class labels), and scrolls the contextual handoff into view on arrival; no implicit save, foreign-class UDA association or source payload propagation is permitted.

Student sharing and simulation require a verified explicit test and class selection; the shared test catalog, S1 UDA scope, editor drafts and independent batch grade import remain authoritative and cannot be altered by Padlet choices.

The optional local Docente OS projection preview must validate a versioned professional JSON before any action, reconcile all real classes without ambiguity and refresh at the serialized planning commit; a user action and durable save are required before showing success, without altering UDA authority or planning draft privacy.

Import of online outcomes to canonical grades requires explicit class, test, assessment period and teacher-selected destination UDA (or an explicit no-UDA decision); historical UDA provenance is never inferred from the mutable current test. A teacher-reviewed preview is bound to the exact current persisted snapshot, and class/student identity must be unambiguous. Only submissions for the selected class and test may create grades. Duplicate IDs, stale test title/question-count metadata, missing/foreign destination UDA, ambiguous identity, invalid score/date, duplicate submission identity and prior grade conflicts fail closed without deleting submissions or overwriting teacher modifications; repeated unchanged imports are no-ops. Existing secure mutation and FLOW-03 completion boundaries remain authoritative, and test sharing cannot authorize imports. INT-02/S2b remains a separate future decision.

An assessment may gain the optional minimal permanent Biblioteca source reference only after an explicit teacher confirmation and a fresh ready, professional, class-matched source check inside the serialized durable test mutation. Editing preserves immutable historical provenance even after source revocation, unauthorized reassignment fails closed, old tests and backups stay compatible, corrupted provenance rejects restore across v2-v6/legacy, file imports never infer origin, and student projection removes private source metadata without affecting UDA, grade import, or deployment.

A Copilot-generated assessment proposal must be a strictly validated, bounded, structured and session-only draft. The parser rejects authority-bearing properties such as assessment IDs, class/UDA/source identifiers, source provenance or a persisted/saved flag, as well as malformed questions or answer keys. Projection exposes only editable title, description and questions, without write authority or changing the existing explicit teacher-save boundary. CREATE_ASSESSMENT remains unsupported until the independent generation and editor handoff gates are qualified; no provider call, Vault write, grading or automatic publication is authorized by this slice.

Remote assessment draft generation is a separate opt-in TEACHER_PROFESSIONAL route, limited to explicitly selected ready professional text sources and a confirmed active class. Its request excludes student identity, UDA/grade/test IDs, binary attachments, provenance and write authority; the server rejects unknown fields and unsafe classifications before provider invocation, applies bounded timeout, AI budget and duplicate-request controls, and parses generated output through the immutable S3a draft validator. The client revalidates the live source and class after remote completion and never saves, grades, shares or publishes. CREATE_ASSESSMENT remains UNSUPPORTED in the Copilot UI until a separately qualified S3c handoff; Vercel deployment stays off.

A generated assessment draft can only cross into the existing editor as a local, transient, teacher-confirmed prefill. A uniquely identified active class pinned to its original class ID even if recreated under the same name, unchanged professional source ID and source content, live Vault state and strict S3a output validation are required. The editor handoff carries no test ID, UDA assignment, grades, saved flag or permanent provenance; dirty drafts and active saves cannot be overwritten. Revalidation is required before the eventual UI delivery. This increment adds no UI, no implicit save, no remote dispatch and no permission to merge or deploy.

The Copilot assessment action requires a teacher-selected professional ready text source, unique current class ID/name, rejecting duplicate names or IDs before any outbound remote request, explicit remote consent and a separate explicit review/adoption click. Browser-side remote generation has a bounded deadline, a user-initiated cancellation and no silent retry; the teacher must renew consent for another attempt. Successful adoption closes the entire Copilot surface so the editor is accessible. Generated assessment content can only be carried as a local transient proposal to the existing assessment editor. Both App and editor recheck the active class and source; an unsaved draft or save-in-progress is never overwritten, a generated proposal has no UDA assignment, test ID, permanent provenance, grades, automatic save or publication. No Vercel deploy is enabled.

Consigli is an explicit class-scoped teacher judgement surface. Mathematically derived evidence averages are read-only and independent from teacher-approved entry grades, which are saved only after durable local Vault commit. Historical legacy grades remain untouched, council entries are optional in appData backups, malformed/orphaned records reject restore, and destructive replacement from a previous archive requires explicit warning. Draft departures are protected. No automatic scrutiny, AI sharing, merge or deployment.

Dated teacher-authored council sessions are independent from evidence grades and council assessment moments. Creation requires explicit teacher confirmation and a durable encrypted appData write. Every session has stable class-year identity, validated actual date and type; multiple meetings in one period remain distinct, readable after navigation and backup restore. Legacy backups stay valid, corrupted sessions fail closed, and replacement of existing sessions demands explicit warning. No official resolutions, remote sharing, merge or deployment.

The class evidence overview is a live and explicitly dated read-only projection: enrolled students, numeric-evidence students and missing students, total numeric evidence, and saved teacher proposals remain distinct. Valid canonical school year and cutoff confine the time range; invalid calendar dates and duplicate student identities fail closed. Never mutate grades, council assessments or sessions, infer a decision, or claim a frozen session snapshot. CDC-01 compact table and navigation remain unchanged.

Council evidence snapshots v1 are optional, teacher-confirmed, append-only aggregate records associated with an existing class/year/session identity. Preview is read-only; confirmation revalidates current canonical source, cutoff and local capture clock, rejects drift and orphaned sessions, preserves older versions and never mutates grades, assessments or the live S2a view. Capture UTC instant, civil date and offset remain mutually consistent across timezones; source and content digests are local integrity hints, never signatures or anonymization. P1 alone does not authorize persistence, backup, UI, merge or deployment.

Confirmed session snapshots must preserve teacher-confirmed append-only history in encrypted appData and backup v6 without silent loss or schema-version changes. Synchronous backup normalization checks record shape, session identity and revision chain; the active restore path awaits SHA-256 content-digest verification before any Vault write. Existing V2–V6 and legacy backups without snapshots remain readable, while snapshots that disappear or change in replacement require explicit consent. SecureAppStorage validates before appData writes, verifies restored records after readback and uses existing atomic Vault batches. P2 adds no UI snapshot capture, remote storage, merge or deploy.

Council evidence snapshot UI is scoped to an explicitly opened saved session and teacher-chosen cutoff. Preparing a six-aggregate preview never saves; only a distinct explicit confirmation can queue a Vault appData/meta commit, always revalidating stored grades, class/year/session, revision, local capture date/offset and source fingerprint from execution-time committed refs. Pending confirmation blocks session and class changes, failed save never publishes a success or a new historical snapshot, opening sessions never snapshots automatically. Older confirmed revisions remain selectable, no student identities or personal grades are duplicated, retroactive capture does not claim historical provenance, no official minutes, remote transfer, merge or deployment.

The teacher-approved P5 mobile usability rework must prominently compare saved proposal counts in a confirmed immutable council snapshot against the independently dated current class overview, while clearly distinguishing source cutoffs. Other historical and current aggregates remain accessible through disclosure controls, without mutation or silently hiding permanently stored values. The capture time is displayed using the recorded UTC timestamp and captured offset rather than the viewer's present timezone; underlying persisted UTC is unchanged. Prepare, cancel, explicit confirmation, immutable revisions and history remain governed by P3 and Vault invariants; no official minutes or automatic snapshot writes are introduced.

Entering Stampa or Analisi does not silently choose the first saved assessment from the shared catalogue. Teacher explicitly selects a valid existing test for display, or a direct intentional editor/catalogue action provides the identity. A deleted or invalid selected ID fails closed without falling back to another test; switching professional class invalidates hidden choices. Rendering a sheet or item analysis is distinct from selecting a recipient class, sharing a link or authorizing grade import, and never writes a test, vote or UDA. Verify on two synthetic tests in both catalogue orders, mobile 320/390 px, and preserve legacy explicit editor choice.

On a phone, the Copilota floating launcher must never obscure the printable assessment sheet or question item analysis: it yields on the active Stampa/Analisi read-only panels while remaining available on Editor/Condivisione and unaffected elsewhere. The teacher-chosen assessment title is shown on the paper sheet with a neutral subtitle, no unqualified statutory assertion and no software advertisement; instructions must not presume that every test format requires a single marked answer. The existing S4b explicit test selection, no implicit fallback, import/share authorities, grades, encrypted Vault and application persistence remain unchanged. Validate Chromium at 390px and 320px with synthetic tests and usable access to other Copilota surfaces. On A4 output, the selected printable assessment is isolated from the application's dark navigation chrome and underlying background, retaining a white paper sheet; other sections' print styles must not be affected.

For a teacher opening the assessment Copilot, present the current class/material, one pedagogical objective, explicit per-attempt approval of external transmission, and one primary action per stage. Hide competing generic Continue/extra source creation controls while the assessment is open, collapse provider and item-level details by default, and preserve the sole explicit transition to an unsaved editable assessment. No persistent assessment, provenance, grade or UDA can be inferred or saved from preview; scope the privacy disclosure to the exact outbound request. Chromium at 390/320px must show no overlay/overflow.

A synthetic teacher cycle through Prepara, explicit test creation and sharing, student submission, scoped Registra import with cancel-before-confirm, and Rivedi must preserve class/test identities and teacher authority. No implicit UDA, grade or provider, and reimport cannot overwrite an unchanged grade. Existing S3c Copilota mocked-provider unsaved draft evidence stays independently required; this adds tests only.

Android HPR is served only by a separate synthetic-only Express entrypoint, with no application product modifications. It requires explicit mode, strong Basic authentication, pinned exact deployed SHA and bounded expiry. Only a predetermined fictional assessment may be processed through the existing policy/consent validation with an in-process fake provider; all other APIs, access without credentials and external assets are blocked. Never enable a real provider or reuse a live Registro Docente deployment. The portable Termux package must be compiled on a pinned CI commit, include a sealed SHA-256 manifest, use a Node-only offline runtime bound exclusively to 127.0.0.1, derive its local password in Termux, expire within three days after first launch, and require no external hosting or remote AI.

The teacher's primary source action opens the existing Copilota assessment proposal flow with the currently selected professional source and class, without requiring a UDA and without navigating directly to the manual editor. Manual S1 source-to-editor handoff remains accessible as an explicit disclosed alternative. The single-attempt provider consent, live source/class guard, unsaved editor and Android Back guard remain authoritative; no automatic saving or real-provider activation is introduced. The modal handoff must not restore keyboard focus to the source card behind the active Copilota, and inherited library tests must explicitly expand the secondary-actions disclosure. On primary Copilota dismissal before editor navigation, restore keyboard focus to the stable, still-visible source «Usa» button; no focus may remain on detached elements.
